context.root_cause: count-based penalty scoring: every LOW finding subtracts 5 points, so a large estate with 13-14 best-practice items (BIMI, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, CAA, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) scored the same as 13 exploitable bugs
context.fix: scoring model now distinguishes exploitable risk from checklist hygiene; INFO for best-practice-only items; no critical/high findings can no longer grade below C; repeated same-class findings no longer stack without bound
context.why_this_posts_well: it is verifiable, it is self-critical, and it proves the product has a real quality pipeline instead of a marketing pipeline

f_grade_audits.grammy.com (Lullabot client): F/40 - DMARC p=none (MEDIUM), BIMI, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, CAA, missing HSTS (MEDIUM)

posts.text:
1/4 We ran our own perimeter scanner against 10 of the biggest web agencies in the world.

4 got an F.

Not one of those F's came from a takeover or an exposed secret. They came from a missing BIMI record and a DMARC policy still in monitoring mode. 🧥
posts.notes: hook: the absurdity of an F with zero criticals

posts.text:
2/4 The bug was ours, and it was embarrassing:

Our scoring subtracted a flat penalty per finding. So a domain with 13 checklist items scored exactly like a domain with 13 exploitable bugs.

Count-based scoring. On a big estate. That's the whole bug.
posts.notes: name the flaw plainly, no spin

posts.text:
3/4 The fix:

• an F now needs real exploit risk, not "missing a nice-to-have"
• best-practice items (BIMI, MTA-STS, CAA) drop to INFO
• repeated findings across subdomains no longer stack
• zero critical/high findings can never grade below a C
posts.notes: proof of engineering, not of marketing

posts.text:
4/4 The proof:

13 rescued from a failing grade.
0 newly failing.
Average +28 points.

We didn't find this because a customer complained. We found it because we graded our own output and asked why a top-tier estate scored like a breach.

→ github.com/CmfH009/Orbit-Security

posts.text:
Security tools have an ego problem: they grade your infra and never admit they're wrong.

Ours graded 4 clean estates F because we count headers, not risk. Fixed today — an F now needs real exploit risk.

Open source: github.com/CmfH009/Orbit-Security

We re-scored all 52 audits we'd ever sent to prospects.

13 were rescued from a failing grade. 0 newly failed. Average +28 points.

Not one F came from a takeover or an exposed secret — they came from a missing BIMI record.
